title: Bee Pollen 20oz (from Nebraska USA)
description: "Bee pollen" refers to the raw pollen pellets collected by worker honey bees. Bee pollen is packed with protein, vitamins, and minerals. The pellets vary in shape, size, and color (according to the kind of flower pollen collected by our bees). Bee pollen has been suggested to aid various medical conditions, since it has antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral properties. For most, it is recommended to start bee pollen consumption in small amounts (gradually working up up to 1 - 2 teaspoons daily). Individuals with pollen allergy, especially severe allergy, should check with their physician before regular bee pollen consumption; everyone's body is unique! Bee pollen can be added to smoothies, cereal, salad, yogurt, granola, ice cream, and a number of other foods.

title: Gallberry Honey 45oz
description: span data-mce-fragment="1"Gallberry honey is a favorite among foodies and chefs as it goes well as a sugar substitute for dishes, pastries and drinks. Its warm and rich honey flavor adds a twist to usual home cooking and baking fare. This honey also has a thick consistency and is known for its lack of crystals (it takes a while for it to crystallize in contrast with other types of honey). This is caused by a high level of diastase enzymes in it which is responsible for preventing Gallberry honey from crystallizing even in cold temperatures./spanbr data-mce-fragment="1"br data-mce-fragment="1"span data-mce-fragment="1"Gallberry usually goes in full bloom during the month of May and can be found growing mostly in the low flatlands of North Carolina, Northern Florida and Georgia. Other sources state that Gallberry, which is harvested from the holly bush, also grows abundantly in the wetlands of Southeast Florida and the Gulf and South Atlantic Coast. This local honey is recommended for people with allergies./span

title: Tupelo Honey 16oz
description:
pNamed as the "champagne of honeys", "Queen of honey", "Southern Gold." Tupelo honey comes from the green-white blossom of the white tupelo gum tree (Nyssa Ogeche). These blossoms are notoriously fragile. In good years, tupelo trees will bloom for only a few weeks. However in a bad year, the nectar flow only in few days./p
pThis raw unfiltered honey comes from the white tupelo trees. The Apalachicola and Chipola river basins, which run from North to South in Gulf County, contain some of the highest concentrations of tupelo trees in the world. The taste is smooth, sweet, light honey with a mild floral and fruity taste. The honey color is light golden amber with a greenish cast. The aroma is cinnamon and floral. This honey, unlike most honeys, resists crystallization and stay as a liquid for years./p

title: Wildflower Honey Sticks (1 lb)

title: Wildflower 45oz
description: span data-mce-fragment="1"Wildflower honey is produced from nectars harvested by bees from a wide variety of flowers. The harvest period runs from April to June during which honeybees would go through a system of flowers to collect nectar from blackberries, tulip poplars, black locusts, maple, basswood and a lot more. This garden variety of wild flowers is what gives wildflower honey its distinct, complex floral flavor. It comes in amber color and has a robust aroma./span

title: Sourwood 16oz
description:
pSourwood honey is highly regarded by honey makers and connoisseurs alike. spanWith a beautiful straw color, the Sourwood texture is smooth and comes across as 'rich' versus a more typically 'sweet' conventional honey. The flavor profile is a soft delicious caramel. /span/p
pSourwood is indigenous to the Southern Appalachians that run across the regions of Northern Georgia and Northwestern Carolina. The trees grow in wild locations - not convenient orchard like settings, and challenges like inquisitive bears or extended rainy periods make for often small, and increasingly rare, honey harvests. Sourwood flowers are white and bell-shaped, and they dangle from branches in clusters that can be a foot long. Sourwood is one of the local honeys that are well recommended for people with regional allergies./p
